title: NetMon: Create pseudo-header if missing
description:
When the 802.11 NetMon dissector is called from USER DLT the "data" parameter to the dissector is null.
In this case we should create an empty header since the main dissection function populates it before calling the 802.11 radio dissector.

notes.body:
> When the 802.11 NetMon dissector is called from USER DLT

Why is it being called from a user DLT?

> the "data" parameter to the dissector is null

Then perhaps you should surround all the code that uses the pseudo-header pointer with

    if (phdr != NULL) {

...

    }

My use case is delivering netmon frames from an extcap plugin.
As far as I understand extcaps should pass pcap/pcapng files to Wireshark and there is no matching "link layer type" for netmon's 802.11 so DLT seemed like a good solution.
I'm open to other suggestions if you have any. 

Regarding  the "!= null" suggestion, that would help prevent the current access violation when the the dissector is called without 'data' but will render the dissector pretty much useless as it mostly populates the header struct and then passes it to 802.11.
I'm not sure if 802.11 can handle a null but even if so, we have information in netmon's header which is crucial for it to dissect correctly so why not pass it along?
Maintainers - Is there anything more I can do to make this merge happen?

> Regarding the "!= null" suggestion, that would help prevent the current access violation when the the dissector is called without 'data' but will render the dissector pretty much useless as it mostly populates the header struct and then passes it to 802.11.

To which dissector are you referring?  The NetMon 802.11 dissector?  Unless you are providing 802.11 radio metadata, the dissector ***IS*** useless - if you have 802.11 frames with no radio metadata, the correct LINKTYPE_ value to use is LINKTYPE_IEEE802_11, and then you just bypass the NetMon 802.11 dissector.

If you *do* have 802.11 metadata to provide, then one solution requiring *zero* changes to Wireshark is to provide one of the "802.11+radio metadata" LINKTYPE_ headers as listed on [the link-layer header types page](https://www.tcpdump.org/linktypes.html).  There's [the radiotap header](https://www.radiotap.org), as used with LINKTYPE_IEEE802_11_RADIOTAP , which has become somewhat of a *de facto* standard for 802.11 radio metadata as generated by UN\*X drivers and by the Npcap driver; there's also [the AVS header](http://web.archive.org/web/20040803232023/http://www.shaftnet.org/~pizza/software/capturefrm.txt), as used with LINKTYPE_IEEE802_11_AVS.

I feel I wasn't clear enough with my intensions and solution. I'll try to be more explicit:

As far as I understand, the NetMon 802.11 dissector (`dissect_netmon_802_11`) expected a non-null ```void* data``` argument.  
More specifically, it assumed `data` is a `struct ieee_802_11_phdr`.  
But unlike the 802.11 dissector (and others) it **does not expect the `data` structure to be populated**. In fact, most of the code within ```dissect_netmon_802_11``` is populating fields of the struct from the NetMon header fields it itself is going to parse (like the radiotap dissector does, but obviously with a different format).

The way the `struct ieee_802_11_phdr` in `data` is created and given to the NetMon 802.11 dissector is as follows:  
1. [It's created in the netmon.c file, parser of NetMon .cap files](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/wiretap/netmon.c#L1016) with default values (mostly zeros anyway except FCS which gets '-2'. I believe this is treated like '-1' [which means "unknown"](https://github.com/wireshark/wireshark/blob/03d6f39a995f49ef48614937da901febf172341f/wiretap/wtap.h#L745))
2. from there, all frames (those containing IEEE 802.11 and others) are passed to [packet-netmon.c, the general NetMon header dissector](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/wiretap/netmon.c#L1438)
3. This dissector simply [copies the pseudo header to the pinfo](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/epan/dissectors/packet-netmon.c#L440) and calls the NetMon 802.11 dissector (via the `wtap_encap_table`)

My point is - none of the components before the NetMon 802.11 insert any valuable information into the struct and allocating a zero'd struct if it's null (like my commit does) gives almost identical results (FCS aside, but it's really not an issue).

Now, the reason I wish NetMon's dissector would run and not radiotap's is I'm using NetMon's API (nmapi.dll and it's underlying driver) to capture traffic.  
It gives me back the entire NetMon 802.11 frame with the IEEE 802.11 frame encapsulated in it.  
I don't want to "translate" the NetMon header to a radiotap header because that feels silly when Wireshark is already capable of parsing this header.  
I also don't want to simply remove the NetMon header and use LINKTYPE_IEEE802_11 with the raw 802.11 frames because it's just throwing interesting information away (like 'center frequency', 'RSSI', 'Operation Mode', ...)

My main goal is to allow (using an extcap plugin) some IEEE 802.11 sniffing on Windows since [npcap has an open issue since 2018 with monitor mode sniffing](https://github.com/nmap/npcap/issues/79) (Which as far as I know is the only way to capture IEEE 802.11 packets with it). You're probably aware of that since I saw some of your comments in github :)

I Hope this clears things up.

> As far as I understand, the NetMon 802.11 dissector (`dissect_netmon_802_11`) expected a non-null `void* data` argument.

Fixed in !2599 - it no longer cares about its argument, it has its own pseudo-header on the stack and fully fills it in by itself, the same way the radiotap etc. dissectors do.

Note that if you're going to have it called for non-NetMon file packets, the dissector *has* to do the entire job of filling in the pseudo-header (while working on this change, I had a version that *didn't* initialize it, and it misdissected packets).

> I don't want to "translate" the NetMon header to a radiotap header because that feels silly when Wireshark is already capable of parsing this header.

But you want users to have to configure your LINKTYPE_USER*n* value in order to use the extcap.

The alternatives are:

1. translate to radiotap (Npcap generates a radiotap header from information supplied to its driver);
1. get a LINKTYPE_ assigned for the raw NetMon header data.
